preconditions.expression: n == int(stdin.split()[0]) and len(stdin.split()[1]) == n and n >= 1 and n <= 2000000
preconditions.description: The first line of stdin is an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 2·10^6) representing the length of the text. The second line is a string of exactly n lowercase Latin letters.

preconditions.expression: all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in stdin.split()[1])
preconditions.description: All characters in the text are lowercase Latin letters (a-z).

postconditions.description: The output is the count of all unique unordered pairs of subpalindromes that cross each other, modulo 51123987. A subpalindrome is defined as a substring of the text that is a palindrome. Two subpalindromes cross if their intervals [start1, end1] and [start2, end2] overlap but neither is completely contained within the other (i.e., start1 < start2 < end1 < end2 or start2 < start1 < end2 < end1).

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= start <= end < n for (start, end) in get_subpalindromes(stdin.split()[1]))
postconditions.description: Every subpalindrome is represented by a pair (start, end) where start and end are 0-based indices in the text, and start ≤ end.

postconditions.expression: all(stdin.split()[1][start:end+1] == stdin.split()[1][start:end+1][::-1] for (start, end) in get_subpalindromes(stdin.split()[1]))
postconditions.description: Every subpalindrome (start, end) is a valid palindrome substring of the text.

postconditions.expression: count_crossing_pairs(text) == sum(1 for i in range(len(subpalindromes)) for j in range(i+1, len(subpalindromes)) if do_cross(subpalindromes[i], subpalindromes[j]))
postconditions.description: The count is computed by checking all unique unordered pairs of subpalindromes and counting those that cross. The function do_cross((s1, e1), (s2, e2)) returns True if the intervals [s1, e1] and [s2, e2] overlap but neither is contained within the other.
The output is the result modulo 51123987.
